## What code will check of you (continued from handoff-keys.md)

`<T>` is your ticket, `<ID>` your dispatch id, `<home>` the project's qa-factory folder - all three stand in your prompt (`Ticket: ... Dispatch: ...`) and in your task packet.

- [execution_request:profile] The execution profile of the run is known without a guess: a profile named by `--profile` or a manifest row's `profile_id` is one `qa-factory/config.json` holds; the asked cases run under one profile; a row that names no profile and whose file lies under another profile's test root, or a root several profiles share, names its `profile_id`; when nothing else tells, `--profile` names it. Door: `profile_id` on the manifest row through `manifest_put.py --fragment`, or `--profile ID` (only where the caller takes it: `run_suite --mine`, never `probe_by_code`); cases of two profiles: one `--mine` per profile.
- [execution_request:profile_command] The profile's one-test command in `qa-factory/config.json` is readable: `commands.one_test.argv` present and in shape, its `env` in shape, and a `selectors.join` rule (when the profile has one) of the form `{"option", "separator", "group"?}`. Door: report it in your digest as an onboarding gap, and write this one run with `run_suite.py --template request`.
- [execution_request:sandbox] A run in a sandbox clone runs in the profile's own directory inside the clone: the profile's `commands.one_test.cwd` (when set) lies inside the project root; the sandbox root is a directory; the run directory resolves inside the clone (no link out of it) and exists there; and every test file the run needs is a file the clone holds. Door: name it as `tooling` in your digest (the card's rule for an incomplete probe); a test file the clone lacks: add it to the repository or run the probe on a tracked copy - see **F-P2-5**.
- [execution_request:scope] A dispatch runs only the cases it was given: every asked case is in the dispatch's scope (a stale live check of a qa-code-critic red probe is admitted by code; anything else passes only on a person's recorded word). Door: hand the case back in your digest; the conductor dispatches it or records the person's word (`waiver.py`, block "outside its scope").
- [execution_request:selector_args] A manifest row of a profile that does not run pytest carries `selector_args` (the framework's own arguments) and `report_test_id`, unless the factory can build the selection from a `run_forms` direct form. Door: give the row `selector_args` and `report_test_id` through `manifest_put.py` once; until then run through `--template request`.
- [execution_request:stand] The stand the run would stand on can be looked at now, and it runs this story's build. Door: name it as `environment` in your digest (`stand_health.py --probe --env <environment>`); a stand that runs another build: the person's word at the build question of the stage entry.
- [execution_request:stand.probe] The story's first typed run on a profile has a way to identify the stand: an `execution.runtime_probes` entry for the profile (or `*`) with an `argv`, or an earlier typed run of the story on the profile to copy the probe from. Door: the probe write command the refusal prints when there is one (`runtime_probe.py --suggest --write --profile <p>`), else write this one request from `run_suite.py --template request` (every later `--mine` copies its probe).
- [execution_request:stand.reference] The story's record does not name its own stand (`pipeline.json` `environment`) as the reference (old version) of a side as well. Door: tell the conductor in your digest which stand runs the new version (the record is corrected by `stage_done.py --set sides.<side>.reference=...`, a conductor command - F-W2).
- [execution_request:window_first] A run that picks part of a case (`--node-id`) does not leave tests of the same file in the dispatch's scope that have never run in this window: one call runs them together. Door: run the command the answer names (`run_suite.py --mine <cases>`); only what a repair touched: `--purpose repair_verify`; this exact run once more: `--again`.
- [run_suite:begin] A request's `idempotency_key` is new, or names the very request (same digest) already recorded under it; a key another process is claiming at the same moment is not reused. Door: write the request with a new `idempotency_key` (a `--mine` run takes a key of its own: run it again); a claim that cannot be read: `--recover <key> --task <T>`.
- [run_suite:phantom_story] `--task` names a story that exists (for `--detail`, `--wait` and the untyped run). Door: the task id of your prompt.
- [handoff_check:binding] Each failure of the run report has at most one triage row and each triage row answers one failure: a row that names several failures is a verdict for none of them, and several rows for one failure keep one - on both paths of the S7 form (its repair list empty or not). Door: triage every failure in `work/triage.json` with ONE row under that failure's own `instance_id`, then run this check again.
- [handoff_check:investigation] In an S7 investigation dispatch the form hands nothing for repair and relists no triage row: `scope` and `not_for_repair` are each an empty list (or absent). Door: write `scope: []` and `not_for_repair: []`.
- [validate_artifacts:check_phase_json.triage.json] `triage.json` carries the keys `triage`. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_triage_v0] One triage row per observation, a verdict from its list, and a FLAKY verdict only with enough reruns, a listed mechanism and a `fix_result`. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [guard_pre_tool:*] 23 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
- [stage_guard:*] 8 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
- [host_adapter:*] 6 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
- [role_cli:*] 11 checks of your commands are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door. Run `artifact_producer.py --help`, `manual_capture.py --help`, `place_answers.py --help`, `red_sandbox.py --help`, `walk_session.py --help` before you write an input file: it prints what each command of the script checks.

### Not yet in rows

work/triage.json is read row by row: every row's `verdict` comes from APP_BUG|TEST_BUG|TEST_BUG:collection|ENV_ISSUE|FLAKY|APP_CHANGED|CASE_DEFECT|ASSERT_STRICTER|NOT_EXECUTED|RUNNER_MISREAD_EVIDENCE|NO_DEFECT (NOT_EXECUTED is code's, for a manual check that did not answer; NO_DEFECT is for an observation `<case>#obs<n>` only, `reason` quoting its evidence), and every row's `evidence` is non-empty whatever the verdict. Every row also names its `instance_id` and `attempt_id`. ASSERT_STRICTER costs a `control` block: `result` effect_without_change, `action`, `without`, `observed`, an existing `evidence` file under `evidence/`; `impossible` needs `why`, no ASSERT_STRICTER. RUNNER_MISREAD_EVIDENCE costs a `contradiction` block: `then`, `runner_said`, `evidence` (a text capture of the attempt) and a `quote` from it (300 characters at most). FLAKY costs three more fields, and all three are checked: `reruns` >= 3 isolated executions of that test, counted across every role;`mechanism` from isolation|race|timing|shared_state|teardown|environment|unknown; and `fix_result` fixed or not_fixed. An unfixed flake is not verified, and quarantining it is the person's call at gate B, never yours.
